item.title: SIR row: Will annul EC orders not in keeping with law, says Supreme Court
item.description: The Supreme Court has asked the Election Commission to clarify decision-making processes related to voter roll revisions. It emphasized that decisions should be taken unanimously or by majority among commission members only. Senior advocate Vikas Singh argued for preserving records and scrutiny of the commission's actions. The court will examine allegations of unilateral actions against the Chief Election Commissioner.
item.dc:creator: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA

item.title: Pakistan, Saudi, Turkiye activate Mecca defence pact as Yemen war escalates
item.description: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to enhance military cooperation to address regional security threats. Following recent attacks by Yemen's Houthi group, the three countries will activate collective deterrence measures. The emergency meeting of the Mecca Defence Alliance in Riyadh led to this commitment. Saudi-backed forces are also launching an offensive against the Houthis in Yemen to regain control.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Nepal ends flood search with over 5,000 still missing, including 189 Indians
item.description: Nepal has suspended non-essential search operations after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods that occurred on August 26. The floods resulted in 1,455 deaths, with 5,285 people still unaccounted for, including many foreign tourists. Among the missing individuals are 189 Indians, along with tourists from various other countries. The government has shifted its focus towards reconstruction and rehabilitation efforts rather than continuing search operations.
item.dc:creator: VISHANT AGARWALA

item.title: 86 to 101: Kohli's final ODI window to break Tendulkar's century record
item.description: Virat Kohli is 15 centuries away from becoming the first batter to reach 101 international hundreds, with ODI cricket now his only route to Sachin Tendulkar's record. India have 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs before the 2027 World Cup, while the Asia Cup offers additional opportunities. A possible six-match South Africa series in the new FTP could give India further preparation before the World Cup, but the century chase remains a difficult one.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Rajya Sabha polls: 8 fresh BJP faces for UP, Hardeep Puri among 2 ministers dropped
item.description: BJP has chosen not to renominate Union ministers Hardeep Singh Puri and B L Verma for Rajya Sabha. This decision raises speculation about a possible reshuffle of the council of ministers by PM Narendra Modi. Since several ministers have been given organization roles, it indicates their continuation in government may be unlikely. Puri's term ends in November, and he may be reassigned for the Punjab assembly polls.
item.dc:creator: KUMAR RAKESH

item.title: In 2009, Google’s Eric Schmidt bought a ship; by 2022, it mapped 1.3m sq km of seafloor
item.description: In 2009, Eric and Wendy Schmidt took a significant step in marine conservation by acquiring a fisheries protection vessel, rebranding it as Falkor. This vessel became a hub for oceanographic research and exploration, hosting over 1,000 scientists and charting more than 1.3 million square kilometers of the ocean by 2022.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Delhi Police ACP's additional DCP charge withheld amid harassment inquiry
item.description: Delhi government modified an order regarding duty charges of 12 police officers after harassment allegations surfaced. Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat voluntarily stepped aside from his additional charge as the inquiry continues. The CDC assignment began prior to the allegations, ensuring it does not indicate a promotion. The complaints have been transferred to the Crime Branch for a detailed investigation and fair inquiry.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Woman declares Rs 67.4L ancestral jewellery in ITR; gets notice, she wins in ITAT
item.description: The assessment threw up two separate issues. The first concerned jewellery worth Rs 67,39,949 that the woman had disclosed in Schedule AL of her income tax return. The tribunal also examined whether the Rs 12 lakh paid to the HUF represented a genuine brokerage expense when the same person, the HUF's Karta/coparcener, had already received another Rs 12 lakh for the same transaction.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Proposed GST changes positive for business: Experts
item.description: Proposed changes to the GST regime are expected to benefit businesses, improving cash flow and refunds. A refund on accumulated GST for input services and capital goods may help manufacturers significantly. The GST Council will discuss the rationalization of ITC, which has long been an issue for businesses. Decriminalization of certain GST provisions aims to create a more business-friendly environment in India.
item.dc:creator: SIDHARTHA

item.title: India-US trade talks have reached plateau: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman
item.description: Negotiations regarding the bilateral trade agreement between India and the US have stalled, reaching a plateau. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that both sides face difficulties in making further concessions. The US aims to reduce its trade imbalance with India, while recent laws have complicated matters. Discussions included tariffs impacting agricultural imports and energy purchases from the US.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Drishyam 3 dips on Day 4, crosses Rs 300 crore worldwide
item.description: Drishyam 3: The Conclusion has achieved over Rs 300 crore in worldwide gross collections shortly after its release. Following a strong opening weekend, the film saw a significant drop in earnings on Monday. Its total net collection in India reached Rs 197.50 crore, while overseas collections contributed an additional Rs 66 crore. The film recorded nearly 8 million footfalls across India within the first four days of its release.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Devil's Sinkhole grows by 1,218 acres after 41 years, tops 3,000 acres
item.description: Texas has significantly expanded the Devil’s Sinkhole State Natural Area, adding 1,218.9 acres to enhance visitor accessibility. The area now spans a total of 3,078.6 acres, including parts of the former Whitworth Ranch. Future developments may introduce around 10 miles of trails aimed at hiking and birdwatching, along with potential facilities like a headquarters and camping sites. This initiative will help preserve natural resources and provide greater recreational opportunities.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Linton-on-Ouse fears becoming 'ghost town' over 1,200 asylum seeker plan
item.description: Linton-on-Ouse residents fear their North Yorkshire village could become a “ghost town” if plans to house 1,200 asylum seekers at the former RAF base proceed. Some homeowners have put properties on the market, warning they could face losses of up to 20%, while residents say empty homes and uncertainty are already affecting the community.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Marc Benioff, wife gave $100M to UCSF; 5 years later, children’s hospital opened
item.description: Marc Benioff and Lynne Benioff significantly contributed $100 million to UCSF for a new children's hospital. This hospital opened in February 2015, featuring advanced facilities designed exclusively for pediatric care. In addition, they made another $100 million donation in 2014 to further support pediatric research and clinical programs. The hospitals were renamed to honor the Benioffs for their generous contributions to children's health care.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Why do people say 'Roger that'? Who was Roger?
item.description: The word 'Roger' has its origins in early military radio communication, symbolizing the letter R and indicating that a message has been received. Its adoption simplified phrases for quick comprehension during transmissions, evolving into a term of competence in popular media. 'Roger that' has since become a common confirmation phrase, though its meaning remains intact.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Kheri case: UP changes PP; SC asks Allahabad HC CJ to decide on trial judge
item.description: The Uttar Pradesh government informed the Supreme Court about replacing the public prosecutor in the Lakhimpur Kheri case. This decision was made in response to allegations raised against the outgoing prosecutor by a witness involved in the case. As the Supreme Court monitors the trial's progress, it was noted that 86 witnesses have been examined thus far.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Only 15% going to work use public transport: NSO
item.description: The National Household Travel Survey indicates that only 15% of workers use public transport for commuting. It reveals that 46% of workers rely on two-wheelers and cars, leading to traffic congestion. Walking is the second most common commute mode, with 28.3% of workers traveling on foot. Student commuting patterns differ significantly, with 37% walking to educational institutions.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35m mansion: Why does it have a $1.75m twin in Illinois?
item.description: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion, Moyenage, has a fascinating architectural connection to a $1.75 million home in Wheaton, Illinois. Both properties were designed by architect Jarvis Hunt for steel magnate Jay C. Morse, with the Ohio estate reportedly based on his earlier Illinois residence. The 10,000-square-foot House of Seven Gables retains historic details, including fireplaces, oak panelling, beamed ceilings and carved woodwork, despite being relocated in 2017.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Naomi Osaka’s family mission: How did her Haitian roots inspire her work?
item.description: Naomi Osaka's heartfelt bond with Haiti is rooted in her family's foundation, which was formed in 1999 to uplift the community. Her inaugural trip to Haiti occurred in October 2017, followed by another visit after her first Grand Slam win in 2018. Engaging with local children, she championed educational initiatives and allocated part of her earnings for earthquake relief. This connection deeply influences Osaka's ongoing philanthropic endeavors.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: In a record, over 10,000 women clear JEE-Advanced
item.description: Women's success rate in JEE-Advanced achieved a record high in 2026 while their IIT seat share remained mostly unchanged. A total of 10,107 women qualified, reflecting a 7.5% increase in their qualifying count. Admissions across IITs reached 18,861, with 20% allocated to female candidates. Significant gains were reported for SC and ST candidates in qualification rates.
item.dc:creator: MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN

item.title: Mission Shakti: How India’s 2019 anti-sat missile test in space caught US off guard
item.description: India conducted an unexpected anti-satellite missile test in 2019, which surprised US security agencies completely. The former NRO officer David Grusch recounted his experiences during the incident on a podcast. India announced its capability after destroying a defunct satellite, making it the fourth country to achieve such technology. This test led to concerns about debris affecting US satellites in orbit.
item.dc:creator: SURENDRA SINGH

item.title: India, Switzerland eye deeper ties in trade, investment, tech
item.description: India and Switzerland have signed five agreements to strengthen cooperation in trade and mobility. The two countries aim to enhance market access for Indian exports and attract Swiss investments in key sectors. A new mobility agreement will facilitate easier access for Indian professionals and students to Switzerland. Both leaders discussed global conflicts and emphasized the importance of dialogue for peace.
item.dc:creator: SACHIN PARASHAR

item.title: Supreme Court agreed to meet, then changed mind: ONOE panel chief
item.description: The Supreme Court initially planned an informal meeting with the parliamentary committee on simultaneous elections. However, the meeting was canceled after opposition MPs raised concerns about the appropriateness of the interaction. The Supreme Court expressed that discussing the matter could lead to future judicial review. The proposal for the meeting was suggested by DMK MP P Wilson.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Pahalgam handler rallies LeT support via anti-Israel rhetoric
item.description: Saifullah Kasuri made controversial remarks regarding the Pakistan army's role in regional conflicts. He threatened to erase Israel from the world map and defend Saudi holy sites. After the Pahalgam attack, he has been active in public events to raise support. High-level meetings between Lashkar-e-Taiba and Hamas have been reported, indicating growing connections. Kasuri's actions reflect an increasing boldness post-attack, as he recruits youth and gathers funds.
item.dc:creator: RAJ SHEKHAR JHA

item.title: Visa doesn't create absolute right to enter India, says Delhi High Court
item.description: The Delhi High Court emphasized that foreign nationals do not have an inherent right to enter India. Justice Amit Mahajan pointed out that holding a visa does not ensure unconditional admission. The court noted various factors that could lead to denial of entry, including national security and public health. A plea by a Turkmenistan woman for reasons regarding her entry refusal was dismissed.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Legislative privilege vs free speech: Supreme Court 7-judge bench may close case
item.description: Nearly 23 years after the Tamil Nadu assembly's breach of privilege resolution, a Supreme Court hearing is scheduled. The resolution imposed a 15-day sentence on some journalists but has since been withdrawn. Senior advocates claimed that the writ petition's cause of action no longer exists and argued the matter has become academic. As a result, the Supreme Court is expected to dispose of the petitions.
item.dc:creator: DHANANJAY MAHAPATRA

item.title: World entering age of flux, India will rise to challenges: EAM S Jaishankar
item.description: S Jaishankar emphasized the uncertainties facing the world during his speech at the Kautilya Economic Conclave. He expressed confidence in India's ability to navigate challenges such as conflicts and economic volatility. The minister highlighted India's proactive stance during crises, including the COVID-19 pandemic and ongoing geopolitical tensions. Jaishankar called for diplomacy to resolve the Russia-Ukraine conflict, particularly concerning maritime security.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Not now daal-ing, says MAGA, as Montana governor comes to India to sell pulses
item.description: Montana's Governor Greg Gianforte is heading a delegation to India to promote agricultural exports. The focus is on selling lentils, peas, and chickpeas to the world's largest consumer of pulses. This trip highlights the growing tension within the Republican party regarding international trade and immigration. Many in the GOP criticize Gianforte's outreach to India amidst concerns about jobs for Americans.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Two killed, Indian among injured after Russian drone hits Turkish cargo ship
item.description: A Russian drone struck the MV Royad Mammadov cargo vessel in the Black Sea, resulting in two fatalities. Among the crew were three Indian nationals, one of whom sustained injuries and received medical care. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy confirmed that the ship's captain was killed in the attack and expressed condolences. Romanian authorities responded to the incident by rescuing 11 crew members and recovering two deceased individuals.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Rawat seeks meet with Congress brass as Kumari Selja slams his yatra plan
item.description: Harish Rawat's thanksgiving yatra has prompted a strong response from AICC, emphasizing the need for party unity. Kumari Selja has criticized the yatra as a parallel program that undermines Congress interests. The party leadership has expressed concern regarding Rawat's controversial statements and the potential division of support. A meeting between Rawat and Selja is expected to take place later this week.
item.dc:creator: SUBODH GHILDIYAL

item.title: Supreme Court may get 3 judges today, to be one short of full strength
item.description: The Union law ministry has announced the appointment of three judges to the Supreme Court. Justice Sunita Agarwal, Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya, and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh have been elevated. These judges were previously chief justices of their respective high courts and will be sworn in soon. With these appointments, the Supreme Court remains one judge short of its sanctioned strength.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Form 6 not modified, only declaration added: Election Commission
item.description: Election Commission officials clarified that there was no change to Form 6, only an additional declaration form was introduced. This statement followed CJI Surya Kant's observation regarding the approval of modified Form 6. Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi accused the Chief Election Commissioner of making illegal changes to the form. The Election Commission denied these accusations and referred to a previous press note for clarification.
item.dc:creator: BHARTI JAIN

item.title: Probe sex assault case against Nagina MP Azad, court directs Delhi cops
item.description: A Delhi court has ordered the completion of an inquiry into a sexual assault complaint against Chandrashekhar Azad. The complainant accused Azad of raping her under the pretext of marriage and claimed the police did not register an FIR. The police sought additional time for the inquiry, but the complainant opposed this request. The court rejected the police's plea and emphasized that the alleged offence is punishable with life imprisonment.
item.dc:creator: KOUSHIKI SAHA

item.title: 'Judicial impropriety': Ex-CJI Gavai on SC judge Bhuyan's remarks criticising SIR
item.description: Justice Ujjal Bhuyan raised concerns regarding the deletion of voters through special intensive revision, facing criticism from former CJI BR Gavai. While Bhuyan emphasized that disenfranchising citizens violates constitutional rights, Gavai expressed reservations about commenting on ongoing legal matters. Former Supreme Court judge Rohinton Fali Nariman also voiced concerns about the democratic implications of voters being removed from lists.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: NCW issues safety guidelines to step-up monitoring of app-based transport services
item.description: The National Commission for Women has released guidelines aimed at improving safety for women passengers using app-based transport services. These measures include verifying the background of drivers and ensuring proper identification matches. Additionally, the guidelines address issues related to late-night travel and unauthorized changes in drivers or vehicles. Aggregators are encouraged to create a verified pool of women drivers to enhance safety.
item.dc:creator: AMBIKA PANDIT

item.title: 'Misleading': EC fact-checks Rahul Gandhi's 'CEC changed Form 6 illegally' post
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: J&K HC quashes PSA detention of Shopian man for ‘showing anti-national tendencies’
item.description: Jammu & Kashmir high court has quashed the preventive detention of Mashooq Ahmad Shah under the Public Safety Act. The court found the allegations against him to be vague and lacking necessary details. Justice Rajnesh Oswal ruled that his detention violated constitutional guarantees under Article 22(5). Shah had been accused of anti-national activities without sufficient evidence. Consequently, the court directed his immediate release if not wanted in other cases.
item.dc:creator: NASEER GANAI

item.title: Scribes covering protests should carry ID, maintain distance: Delhi Police advisory
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: Congress 'elevates' Imran Masood: Muslim outreach or message to Akhilesh?
item.description: In Uttar Pradesh, Congress is setting the stage for the 2027 assembly elections amidst complicated alliance dynamics with the Samajwadi Party. The selection of Imran Masood as state chief has ignited concerns about Congress's approach to the alliance and the contentious seat-sharing talks. Masood's clear statements on the party's electoral strategy suggest underlying tensions that might define their coalition's effectiveness in challenging the BJP.
item.dc:creator: KUNAL VARMA

item.title: Chirag Paswan's UP gamble: Why PM Modi's 'Hanuman' is flexing his muscle against allies
item.description: Chirag Paswan's decision to contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election marks an expansion of LJP (Ram Vilas). With plans to prepare for all 403 seats, the move could test the party's ability to build a Dalit vote base, influence close BJP-SP contests and strengthen its bargaining power within the NDA. His political journey from the 2020 Bihar split to a 19-seat win in 2025 provides the backdrop.
item.dc:creator: PALLAVI

item.title: Saudi-led coalition targets Red Sea territory held by Houthis. What's Pak's role?
item.description: Islamabad has not publicly acknowledged direct involvement in Saudi Arabia's offensive inside Yemen. However, several reports point that Pakistani forces could be helping Saudi Arabia shift more of its military resources towards the war by taking over defensive responsibilities inside the kingdom. That could allow Saudi forces to concentrate on the offensive against the Houthis without Pakistan formally becoming a combatant in Yemen.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: BJP drops all 8 Uttar Pradesh Rajya Sabha members - what it means
item.description: The outgoing BJP members, apart from Hardeep Singh Puri and BL Verma, are Arun Singh, Neeraj Shekhar, Geeta Shakya, Brijlal and Seema Dwivedi. The eighth seat belonged to former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma, who resigned on September 11 after being appointed lieutenant governor (LG) of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. His term was due to end on November 25, like those of the others.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: No apology, no handshakes from Indian players: Is this why PCB denied NOCs for WCL?
item.description: Pakistan Champions have withdrawn from the World Championship of Legends after the PCB refused to issue NOCs. The withdrawal follows the board's demands for an apology from Indian players concerning past matches. As a result, Pakistan Champions will not be participating in the ongoing season, ending their campaign prematurely. The PCB and WCL could not reach an agreement on several conditions concerning past events.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
